Corollary
[compact manifolds are geodesically complete]

Source: petersen:page-0190 ↗ prop:pet-ch5-leaves-compact-set

1. ch5:5.2.5If $M$ is a compact Riemannian manifold, then for each $p\in M$, $v\in T_pM$ there is a geodesic $c:\mathbb R\to M$ with $c(0)=p$, $\dot c(0)=v$: geodesics exist for all time.
Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch5-leaves-compact-set ↗ lem:pet-ch5-global-uniqueness ↗ thm:pet-ch5-local-existence \sketch Patch the local solutions through $(p,v)$ using section 2; their union is maximal on $(a,b)$. If $b<\infty $, section 2 with $K=M$ would force $c(t)\notin M$ near $b$, impossible. Thus $b=\infty $, and the reversed geodesic gives $a=-\infty $.

□
